data.title: BOJ's Ueda Reaffirms Readiness to Keep Raising Rates
data.description:
By Megumi Fujikawa

TOKYO--Bank of Japan Gov. Kazuo Ueda again reiterated that he is prepared to tighten monetary policy further, reinforcing market views that another interest-rate hike could come as soon as December.

Speaking to a parliamentary committee on Thursday, Ueda said it is important to keep underlying consumer inflation anchored around 2% so that it doesn't overshoot the central bank's 2% target and hurt the economy.

"The bank will continue to raise the policy interest rate and adjust the degree of monetary accommodation, in response to developments in economic activity and prices as well as financial conditions," he said.

Ueda warned that one measure of underlying inflation--consumer prices excluding fresh food--is likely to accelerate clearly above 2% as firms pass on higher labor costs, oil remains expensive and the yen's weakness persists. Surging global demand related to the artificial-intelligence buildout adds another inflationary impulse.

In September, that gauge of underlying inflation accelerated to 2.1% year-on-year from August's 1.7%. Economists polled by data provider Quick expect October data due Friday to show a further rise to 2.3%.

The BOJ said last month that underlying inflation had reached its 2% target for the first time since the goal was introduced in 2013.

Write to Megumi Fujikawa at megumi.fujikawa@wsj.com

data.title: Indonesian fire emissions third highest on record this year, EU's Copernicus says
data.description:
This year's fires in Indonesia produced nearly 200 million metric tons of carbon emissions by November 15, the European Union's climate monitoring service said on Thursday, the third-highest annual volume on record.

  • The archipelago has suffered its worst wildfire season in years, driven by excessively dry super-El Niño weather conditions and warmer temperatures, as well as extensive land clearing

  • Total fire emissions fell short of the record of nearly 400 million tons in 2015 and were also slightly lower than in 2006, another strong El Niño year, according to the EU's Copernicus Atmosphere Monitoring Service (CAMS), which tracks fire emission records dating back to 2003

  • This year's fire emissions were the equivalent of more than a fifth of Indonesia's total carbon footprint in 2025, with the country's energy consumption and industry responsible for an estimated 960 million tons of CO2 last year, according to the Statistical Review of World Energy

  • Emissions generated by Indonesia's fires were also around the same as the entire energy and industrial carbon footprint of Pakistan last year

  • CAMS data showed that nearly 8.9 million hectares (22 million acres) of land could have been damaged by fire in Indonesia this year, 4.7% of its total area, significantly higher than the 2012 to 2025 average of 1.9%.

  • The figure is significantly higher than the 2.9-million-hectare estimate for January to October provided last week by geomonitoring platform Nusantara Atlas, which uses a more conservative methodology

  • Though El Niño-driven drought was a decisive factor in this year's fires, experts have also emphasised the role played by climate change in driving up temperatures

  • Poor land management and the excessive draining of peatland to make way for palm oil or pulpwood concessions have also made Indonesia more vulnerable to fire

data.title: Defence Stocks: HAL, BEL, BDL, peers in the spotlight after ministry seeks 20% hike in FY28 capex
data.description:
Shares of defence companies, including Hindustan Aeronautics Ltd. (HAL), Bharat Electronics Ltd. (BEL), and Bharat Dynamics Ltd. (BDL), will be in focus on Thursday, November 19, after the Defence Ministry reportedly sought a 20% increase in capital expenditure for FY28, potentially to fund major acquisitions.

The proposed spending push could support big-ticket procurement programmes, including the acquisition of 114 Rafale fighter jets and six advanced conventional submarines equipped with Air-Independent Propulsion (AIP) under Project 75I.

India's defence capital expenditure allocation for FY27 stood at ₹2.19 lakh crore, marking a 22% increase over the FY26 Budget estimate of ₹1.8 lakh crore.

The Defence Ministry has signed contracts worth around ₹80,000 crore so far in the current financial year.

Meanwhile, India's defence exports have risen sharply from ₹600 crore to a record ₹38,000 crore. The government's target of achieving ₹50,000 crore in defence exports by 2029 could potentially be met ahead of schedule.

Other key development

The government is expected to announce the winner of the competition to develop prototypes of the Advanced Medium Combat Aircraft (AMCA), India's proposed fifth-generation stealth fighter.

Defence Minister Rajnath Singh has said the selected entity will be a private-sector company or a private-sector-led consortium, potentially involving a public-sector partner.

According to media reports, three groups are competing for the estimated ₹15,000-crore programme:

- Tata Advanced Systems

- Larsen & Toubro (L&T), in partnership with Bharat Electronics Ltd. (BEL) and Dynamatic Technologies

- Bharat Forge, in partnership with BEML and Data Patterns

data.title: dorsaVi Opens New International Sales Channel with LuxingSport French Distribution Deal
data.description:
dorsaVi Limited has signed its first French distribution agreement, opening a new route to overseas customers for its movement-analysis technology without the expense of building a local sales team.

France-based LuxingSport will introduce the Australian technology developer’s products to professional sporting organisations, physiotherapists, and research groups through its existing sales network.

The deal marks the first step in a wider distributor-led expansion across Europe and Asia, with dorsaVi to continue selling directly to customers in Australia and the US.

Initial French sales activity is expected to start in November and December, after which the partners plan a broader market-development campaign during 2027.

French Partner with Reach

Headed by Laurent Massias, LuxingSport already works with the kinds of specialist customers dorsaVi wants to reach.

Massias approached the business several months ago after examining its range of wearable sensors and software used to measure and assess human movement.

Those products have been deployed in elite sport, clinical treatment, and workplace settings, giving dorsaVi an established platform to take into new territories.

The company’s technology has previously been used by organisations including Boeing, Caterpillar, and Medtronic, as well as by professional sporting bodies, existing relationships that are unrelated to the French agreement.

Lite International Expansion

Rather than recruiting and managing a separate salesforce in France, dorsaVi will draw on LuxingSport’s customer relationships and local market knowledge, leaving the company free to concentrate more of its resources on product development, training, and technical support as distributors seek customers on the ground.

“Rather than building large sales teams in every new jurisdiction, we see an opportunity to work with capable distributors who understand their customers and already have established routes to market,” group chief executive officer Mathew Regan said.

“LuxingSport is an encouraging first partner for this approach—its experience in elite sport, physiotherapy, and research aligns well with the customers and applications for which dorsaVi’s products have been developed.”

dorsaVi is looking beyond France to other European countries, Japan, and selected Asian markets where medical technology, rehabilitation, and sports-performance businesses have established distribution networks.

Any additional territories will be considered against customer demand, regulatory requirements, and the capabilities and commercial terms offered by prospective partners.

Flexible Sales Agreement

The French arrangement is non-exclusive and runs initially for 12 months, with automatic annual renewals unless either party provides 90 days’ notice.

LuxingSport will buy dorsaVi products and subscriptions for resale, paying for accepted orders rather than committing to a fixed volume upfront, with no minimum purchase quantities or compulsory inventory commitments and the value of future sales yet to be established.

dorsaVi plans to support the rollout with partner training and commercial assistance while maintaining its own sales relationships in Australia and the US.

The French launch will sit alongside those established operations, rather than replace the sales activities dorsaVi already maintains in its two core markets.

data.title: Indian rupee's inflow-driven upward momentum faces hawkish Fed headwinds
data.description:
By Nimesh Vora

The Indian rupee is expected to open largely flat on Thursday, with sustained foreign equity inflows cushioning it against dollar strength amid hawkish Federal Reserve signals.

The rupee is expected to open little changed after settling at 93.44 to the dollar on Wednesday. It climbed to 93.2450 during the session, its highest level in nearly seven months, before slipping.

Still, the currency remains on an upward trajectory, bankers said, underpinned by foreign equity inflows and a shift in market positioning, with speculators increasingly reluctant to take on dollar-long bets.

On Wednesday, while the rally in Indian equities lost steam, foreign investors continued to buy, pumping more than $600 million into domestic shares. This takes their net purchases so far this month to nearly $12 billion.

The bias on USD/INR remains on the downside; however, the move is likely to be more of a "incremental" move lower, a currency trader at a bank said.

The rupee has already recovered substantially, and further move higher may come at a measured pace, with intermittent bouts of "consolidation and opportunities", he said.

The rupee's recovery is facing an external headwind as Federal Reserve officials signal that the fight against inflation may require a more aggressive policy response.

Minutes of the Fed's October 27-28 meeting, released on Wednesday, showed policymakers increasingly concerned that inflation could prove persistent, with some calling for further tightening.

That hawkish tone was reinforced by Fed Governor Christopher Waller, who said the central bank should either deliver a 50-basis-point rate hike in December or signal a faster pace of increases in 2027.

The remarks are likely to keep the dollar supported, with the currency already trading near a one-and-a-half-year high.

Danske Bank has added a January rate hike to its Federal Reserve outlook, and now expects three further 25-basis-point increases in December, January and March, taking the fed funds rate to 4.50%-4.75%, where it sees rates remaining through the rest of 2027.

data.title: Indonesia's Aneka Petroindo signs deal to buy Vivo petrol stations
data.description:
Indonesia's PT Aneka Petroindo Raya, the operator of BP-AKR petrol stations in the country, has signed a deal to buy a 90% stake in PT Vivo Energy Indonesia, an affiliate of the Swiss-based Vitol Group.

  • The remaining 10% of PT Vivo Energy Indonesia will be acquired by a non-affiliate firm, Aneka Petroindo Raya (APR) said in a statement

  • APR will integrate Vivo's 47 locations into its petrol station operations and plans to rebrand them as BP-AKR stations, according to the statement issued late on Wednesday

  • The overall transaction was valued at $15.5 million, according to a stock exchange filing by APR's parent company AKR Corporindo

  • APR currently operates 75 BP-AKR petrol stations on Java island

  • BP sold its 49.9% stake in APR earlier this month to AKR Corporindo, making AKR the sole owner of the operator

  • The company will continue to use the BP-AKR brand for its petrol stations

  • Indonesia's energy ministry tightened direct fuel imports by private firms last year, resulting in shortages at private fuel stations, including those operated by BP and Shell

  • Shell announced in October that it had completed the transfer of ownership of its Indonesian petrol station business to the SEFAS Group

data.title: Uber Co-Founder Kalanick Teases Protest at Nvidia as Calls for Huang's Return Continue — WSJ
data.description:
By Angel Au-Yeung

Uber co-founder Travis Kalanick walked on stage at an investor conference in Austin, Texas, wearing a black leather jacket. Next to him was Antonio Gracias, close friend and longtime investor of Elon Musk — also in a black leather jacket.

"Yours looks a lot like Jensen's," said Gracias, referring to Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang, who had made a black leather jacket his uniform and was ousted last week as chief executive of the chip maker.

"Yeah, we gotta bring Jensen back," said Kalanick.

Calls from Silicon Valley's elite for Huang's reinstatement continued to reverberate Wednesday, even after Nvidia's board chairman declared that the company has no intention of bringing him back. Huang stepped down last week following reports of affairs with two women, one of whom U.S. officials had suspected was passing information to Chinese intelligence during their relationship.

While on stage at the TomorrowX Summit, Kalanick said he would show up at Nvidia's offices "with a wafer encrusted megaphone" to lead employees on a walkout. "Let's fight for what's right and give it a best shot," he said. "We don't have control of the outcome, but let's f — ing fight."

Kalanick compared Huang's saga to his own fight to remain CEO of Uber before resigning under pressure in 2017. Kalanick couldn't immediately be reached for comment.

Huang's supporters have argued that the former CEO is pro-American and essential to ensuring that the U.S. has a thriving open-source AI ecosystem. They have questioned why he was forced out before an investigation announced by the board delivered its findings.

At the New York Times DealBook Summit, also on Wednesday, the technorati took turns praising Huang.

Musk compared Huang's ouster to "kicking Michael Jordan off your team when you're on a winning streak." The billionaire, who appeared remotely from China, also reiterated past comments he wrote on X that he would hire Huang.

Greg Brockman, president of OpenAI, described Huang as "singular" while OpenAI chief executive Sam Altman said it was "hard to imagine the AI industry without Jensen." Palmer Luckey, founder of Anduril Industries, said that "nobody can take Jensen's place in this critical juncture."

"Has NVIDIA's Board lost perspective?" wrote Ron Conway, venture capitalist and founder of SV Angels, on X. "The Board prejudged him even before their own internal investigation was completed. Why push out a visionary American founder?"

Bill Ackman, founder of Pershing Square, also took to X to lambaste Nvidia's directors. "The board's conduct here is shocking for a company of this scale and importance to our country and the world at large, particularly at this moment in history," he wrote on X.

In Huang's first public remarks on Tuesday since he stepped down, he said he would be willing to return to Nvidia as chief executive if the board believes "my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America."

Write to Angel Au-Yeung at angel.au-yeung@wsj.com

data.title: Gold recovers from over one-year low as markets assess Fed rate outlook
data.description:
Key points:
  • Traders price in 90% chance of a 25-bp Fed hike in December
  • Global Platinum market to swing back to deficit next year
  • Break below $3,800 risks reinforcing bearish sentiment- OCBC analysts

By Sukanya Mitra

Gold prices rose on Thursday after hitting a more than one-year low in the previous session, as investors looked to Federal Reserve commentary for clues on the US interest-rate outlook.

Spot gold was up 0.6% at $3,743.26 per ounce, as of 0240 GMT, after hitting its lowest level since September 2025 in the previous session. U.S. gold futures for December delivery gained 0.1% to $3,744.30.

"It's (Gold) making a mild attempt to lift itself from its 13-month low, but this is more likely to be profit-taking from bears over any fundamental catalyst," said Matt Simpson, senior market analyst at StoneX.

Fed officials saw a growing risk last month that they might need to intensify their efforts to control inflation, even as they agreed to keep interest rates steady for the moment, the minutes of their October 27-28 showed on Wednesday.

Fed Governor Michael Barr said he's likely to be on board with tighter monetary policy in an economy still beset by inflation pressures.

Additionally, Fed Governor Christopher Waller said the US central bank needs to get more aggressive in its response to inflation, and either approve a half-point hike at the December meeting or communicate a faster pace of interest rate increases in 2027.

Markets see a 90% chance of a 25-basis-point US rate hike in December, while the probability of a larger 50-basis-point move is priced at 10%, according to CME's FedWatch tool.

Higher interest rates increase the opportunity cost of holding non-yielding bullion, reducing its appeal to investors.

"The break below $3,800 risks reinforcing bearish sentiment. Buying interest remains subdued, while the continued decline raises the risk of further liquidation," analysts at OCBC said in a note.

Meanwhile, the global platinum market will swing back to deficit next year due to higher bar and coin demand and smaller outflows from platinum-backed exchange-traded funds, the World Platinum Investment Council said on Wednesday.

Spot silver was up 0.6% at $45.27 per ounce, platinum edged 0.1% higher to $1,373.35 and palladium gained 0.7% to $954.60.

data.title: Saudi Aramco issues fuel oil tender for end-November and December loading, sources say
data.description:
Saudi Aramco issued its latest tender to sell high-sulphur fuel oil for loading in late November and December, trade sources said on Thursday.

The company offered a total of 11 HSFO cargoes in a tender issued late on Wednesday, sources said.

This includes seven 600,000-barrel cargoes for loading from Ras Tanura and four 80,000-ton cargoes for loading from Jubail.

Saudi fuel oil supplies appear to have retained a robust pace despite a refinery attack in late October, sources said.

The tender closes on November 23 with validity until November 24, they said.

Saudi Aramco did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

data.title: BOJ's Ueda Reaffirms Readiness to Keep Raising Rates
Asian Equities Decline as Caution Prevails
data.description:
By Ronnie Harui

Asian equities were broadly lower Thursday morning as firmed expectations of higher interest rates inspired little demand for stocks and sentiment stayed cautious.

Investors are digesting hawkish-sounding minutes from the Federal Reserve's October meeting, and looking ahead to the trilateral summit between U.S. President Donald Trump, China's Xi Jinping, and Russian President Vladimir Putin.

"Trump and Xi are also scheduled for a separate bilateral meeting. The meetings represent the highest-level diplomatic engagement in months and will be closely watched for any signals on trade, technology restrictions, and the broader geopolitical framework affecting Asian markets," Commerzbank Research analysts said.

Anthropic's trading debut is also in focus, seen as a major test of appetite for artificial-intelligence trades after the Nvidia scandal sparked another wave of selloffs in the technology sector.

Concerns about the impact of tightened U.S. export restrictions on advanced chips continue to weigh on tech and AI-related stocks in Asia.

Fragile risk sentiment was evident across major indexes.

South Korea's Kospi gave up early gains to turn lower during the morning session, and was recently down 0.9%. Taiwan's Taiex was off by 2.7%, while Chinese benchmarks were in the red. Japan's Nikkei Stock Average swung between gains and losses and was last 0.1% higher.

In Hong Kong, major tech names posted sharp drops, dragging the Hang Seng Tech Index 2.1% lower.

Elsewhere, crude oil futures were mixed after Iran launched strikes against Kuwait and Bahrain on Wednesday, while continuing attacks against ships seeking to pass through the Strait of Hormuz, a key waterway through which one-fifth of the world's oil is transported.

Front-month West Texas Intermediate futures edged 0.1% lower to $83.15 a barrel and front-month Brent rose 0.3% to $92.21 a barrel, ICE data showed.

Gold recovered some ground, rising 0.7%, but stayed around its lowest levels in over on year at $3,750.18 an ounce. Silver also bounced back but stayed weak.

Write to Ronnie Harui at ronnie.harui@wsj.com

data.title: India bonds seen flat as traders await fresh rate cues, debt supply
data.description:
By Dharamraj Dhutia

Indian government bonds are expected to be little changed in early trading on Thursday as traders look for fresh cues on the interest-rate outlook, while awaiting debt supply due a day later.

The benchmark 6.94% 2036 bond (IN069436G=CC) yield is expected to move between 7.26% and 7.32%, according to a private bank trader, after ending at 7.2858% on Wednesday.

"With yesterday's attempt of taking the yield sustainably below 7.25% thwarted, we should see some consolidation in 7.30%-7.32% range," the trader said.

Shorter-dated US Treasury yields rose after minutes from the Federal Reserve's latest meeting showed support for holding rates steady was less broad than the headline 10-2 vote suggested.

"The prospect of a 50bp hike in December was already being raised and has since become more likely following stronger-than-expected payrolls and inflation figures," Capital Economics said in a note.

Treasury yields have stabilised for now, but saw a large upswing last week, with markets fully pricing in a 25-basis-point rate hike by the Fed in December, following stronger-than-expected October inflation data and hawkish comments from US Fed officials.

Crude prices remained steady, but the outlook is still fragile as any prolonged disruption to tanker traffic in the Strait of Hormuz could quickly tighten global supplies.

This remains a risk for energy import-dependent India, as it affects current account deficit pressures, the local currency, and inflation.

The market has been positioned for another Reserve Bank of India rate hike in early December, after India's retail inflation moved above the RBI's 6% upper tolerance threshold for the first time in two years.

Meanwhile, New Delhi will sell bonds worth 330 billion rupees ($3.53 billion) on Friday, which includes the liquid five-year security.

RATES

Overnight index swap rates are also expected to consolidate around current levels.

On Wednesday, the one-year (INR1YMIBROIS=CC) rate ended at 6.5250%, the two-year rate (INR2YMIBROIS=CC) closed at 6.52%, and the liquid five-year (INR5YMIBROIS=CC) rate settled at 6.56%.

($1 = 93.4700 Indian rupees)

data.title: Oil prices steady as supply surplus softens sentiment though Gulf war supports
data.description:
By Colleen Howe

Oil prices were steady on Thursday after falling previously as increasing expectations for a supply surplus and higher interest rates softened sentiment, outweighing support from attacks on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz amid the lingering Iran war.

Brent crude futures were trading up 17 cents, or 0.18%, at $92.12 a barrel as of 0237 GMT. US West Texas Intermediate futures fell 9 cents, or 0.11%, to $83.17.

Brent fell 1.3% in the previous session while WTI dropped 3.2% to its lowest since August 26 on emerging expectations of a supply surplus as crude shipments through the Strait of Hormuz have returned to roughly pre-war levels.

Prices have also come under pressure from expectations of higher US interest rates that would cause lower economic growth and slower demand increases for oil. That would also strengthen the dollar, raising prices for non-US buyers paying for dollar-denominated crude in different currencies.

Minutes from the US Federal Reserve's October meeting, released on Wednesday, bolstered investor expectations that the central bank could raise interest rates at its next meeting in December to control inflation.

"Softer oil prices provide some relief to those concerned about persistent inflationary pressures, although the question is no longer simply whether the Fed will hike rates in December, but by how much. This, in turn, supports the dollar, hindering any attempt by the oil market to rally," analysts at PVM, a brokerage, said in a note dated November 18.

A larger-than-expected rise in US oil stocks reported on Wednesday also weighed on the market outlook.

US crude inventories rose by 3.4 million barrels to 417.8 million barrels in the week ended November 13, the EIA said, compared with analysts' expectations in a Reuters poll for a rise of 58,000 barrels.

Still, risks remain for Middle East oil supply amid the US-Israeli war on Iran.

Iran's navy said three oil tankers sailing east of the Strait of Hormuz were disabled by mines, Iranian media reported on Wednesday.

Markets are awaiting the trilateral summit between the leaders of the US, China and Russia, seeking clues about the prospects of a negotiated end to the US-Iran war and Russia's invasion of Ukraine, which have disrupted global oil markets.

Reuters reported on Wednesday that Ukrainian drone attacks have reduced Russian oil refineries' combined crude processing volumes by 45% since late October, citing industry sources.

data.title: Global commodity prices plunge: These are the metals impacted and Emkay's preferred plays
data.description:
Global commodity markets are experiencing a broad sell-off as a surging US Dollar, mounting Federal Reserve rate hike expectations, and an unwinding of the artificial intelligence infrastructure trade pressure prices across energy, metals, and agriculture.

With the US Dollar Index climbing to a 19-month high on the back of rising inflation and higher US yields, markets are now pricing in a greater than 90% probability of a Federal Reserve rate hike in December 2026.

Crude Oil Prices At Three-Month Low

In the energy market, Brent crude oil prices have dropped to a three-month low, holding near $92 per barrel after tumbling 20% in November alone. Bearish sentiment has been compounded by supply-side pressures, with the US Energy Information Administration (EIA) estimating a 2 million barrels-per-day surplus in Q2 2026. Reinforcing these oversupply concerns, US crude inventories jumped by 3.38 million barrels alongside simultaneous increases in US gasoline and distillate stocks.

Base Metals Impacted

The sharpest declines have hit the metals complex, particularly base metals tied to AI infrastructure buildouts. Despite Nvidia posting strong earnings, its signal toward greater discipline in AI portfolio investments has prompted investors to unwind long positions in the AI trade.

Combined with a sluggish demand backdrop in China, copper prices plunged 5.4% overnight to hit a seven-month low. Prices are now down 13% for the month, thereby wiping out its gains to turn flat for 2026.

Similarly, aluminum slid to a 52-week low after falling 7% in November, while zinc dropped 5% overnight, though it still holds onto a 13% gain for the year. Tin also fell to an eight-month low, declining 8% this month even as exchange inventories tighten, with LME stocks hovering near a one-year low of 3,885 tons and Shanghai inventories down 66% from June to 4,000 tons.

Gold, Silver Sell-Off Continues

Precious and industrial metals have not been spared from the dollar rally and shifting demand trends either. Gold prices fell 3.2% overnight to the lowest since September 2025, bringing its year-to-date decline to 13%, while silver tumbled 4.8% overnight to a 14-month low. The white metal is now down 36% in 2026.

Platinum shed 4.25%, and palladium sank to a 19-month low below $1,000 per ounce as an 8% year-on-year rise in global electric vehicle sales in October 2026 continues to weigh on traditional automotive catalyst demand.

Meanwhile, soft and agricultural commodities followed the broader downward trend, with wheat down 4%, cotton and cocoa losing 3% each, corn hitting 14-week lows, and sugar falling to a two-month low—leaving rice futures as a rare outlier near 2024 highs.

What Next For Metals & Top Stock Picks

Looking at the domestic sector outlook, analysts see diverging fortunes for Indian metals.

Under a bear-case scenario of aluminum and alumina prices at $2,600 and $360 per ton respectively, Emkay prefers Vedanta Aluminium with a fair value of ₹449 (at 6x EV/EBITDA), notes limited upside of 7.2% for Hindalco, and ranks NALCO as its least-preferred pick with a fair value of ₹326.

Conversely, domestic steelmakers appear better insulated; safeguard duties and localized pricing dynamics—with HSBC noting domestic steel trades at a 5% to 6% premium over Chinese imports—position the sector for strong volume growth in the second half of FY27 as domestic demand improves.

Axis Capital notes that global aluminum demand growth slowed to 1.2% year-on-year in the first nine months of 2026, compared to a 3% CAGR between 2023 and 2025, projecting the global market to swing into a 0.5 million tonnes per annum (mtpa) surplus in 2027.

The Nifty metal index was the worst performing index on Wednesday, falling over 2.5%, with nearly all constituents ending the session with losses led by Vedanta Aluminium, which fell 5.5%.

data.title: How safe is your job? Aus economy sheds 43,500 jobs as unemployment hits four-year high
data.description:
Key points:
  • Australia's unemployment rate has risen for three straight months, from 4.5% in July to 4.9% in October – its highest level since October 2021 and a far cry from the labour shortages of the post-pandemic recovery.
  • October's Labour Force survey showed 43,500 jobs lost against economists' forecasts for a 25,000 gain – the second large monthly fall in a row – with part-time workers and young Australians bearing the brunt.
  • We look at where the job losses are falling, why ASX consumer stocks have been warning of exactly this, what the major investment banks expect next, and what it all means for the RBA's December meeting.

For most of the post-Covid period, the labour market was the Australian economy's strongest pillar. Recent data suggests that pillar is cracking. Over the 12 months to October, the number of unemployed Australians rose by 95,400, or 14.5%, while employment grew by just 83,500 – meaning more people joined the jobless queue than found work.

The Australian Bureau of Statistics' (ABS) Labour Force survey released today showed seasonally adjusted employment fell by 43,500 in October, well short of economists' forecasts for a 25,000 increase. It follows September's 36,400 decline, and pushed the unemployment rate to 4.9%, with 753,700 Australians now looking for work.

In this article, we unpack who’s losing their jobs, how corporate Australia has been flagging the slowdown for weeks, and what the economists at the major investment banks expect from here – including what today's numbers could mean for the Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA).

Part-timers first in the firing line

Part-time employment fell by 40,600 in October, while full-time employment slipped by just 2,900. September told the same story: full-time jobs rose by 35,400 while part-time jobs fell by 71,800. Across the two months, that's roughly 112,000 part-time positions gone against a net gain of around 32,500 full-time roles.

Consider that the Australian economy has shed jobs in three of the last four months, and the chart below appears to show a sharp downturn since July (i.e., following the first three of five RBA official cash rate hikes this year).

Australia: monthly change in employment (seasonally adjusted). Source: ABS Labour Force, Australia, October 2026 (seasonally adjusted)

Hours worked fell 0.2% and the participation rate eased to 66.6%. Fewer hours worked means there’s less work to go around – a leading indicator that employers are pulling back on their labour requirements. A falling participation rate, meanwhile, suggests more Australians are becoming discouraged about finding work and stepping out of the jobs market altogether.

Youth unemployment rose to 11.3% from 11.1%, the highest since October 2021, signalling that younger workers are taking the hardest hit. Consider that jobs for new entrants to the workforce are typically the first to go at the beginning of a protracted downturn in hiring.

Corporate Australia saw this coming

ASX companies have been sending a signal for months now that the local economy is beginning to bear the brunt of higher interest rates and a sharp downturn in consumer confidence.

Nick Scali (NCK) told the market on 21 October that Australia-NZ written sales orders fell 15% in the first quarter of FY27, with store traffic down about 10%. The furniture retailer expects first-half revenue for the region to land 11–14% below the prior year.

JB Hi-Fi (JBH) reported a 1.4% fall in comparable sales at JB Hi-Fi Australia for the September quarter, and said sales had slowed in October ahead of Black Friday and Christmas. Customers, it said, remain focused on value and are increasingly holding out for promotional events.

Eagers Automotive (APE) said on 5 November that third-quarter trading in Australia was hit by industry-wide headwinds, citing the elevated interest rate environment, persistent inflationary pressures and higher fuel prices. APE still expects record revenue for calendar 2026, largely on the back of acquisitions.

There are many more. The problem facing Aussie retailers is that margins are being squeezed from both ends. Just yesterday, the ABS reported the wage price index rose 3.5% over the year to the September quarter, above expectations according to Macquarie, which notes the result was largely driven by the Fair Work Commission's 4.75% award wage increase.

Meanwhile, UBS's reading of the latest business confidence survey showed selling prices easing to 2.4% annualised in October while purchase costs remain very high – which the investment bank says implies significant margin compression.

What the experts are saying

Macquarie also noted that SEEK job ad volumes were down 6% year-on-year in October, while applications per ad hit a record 239 in September – i.e., fewer jobs, and more people chasing what’s there. Looking forward, the bank sees limited evidence of a sustained recovery in ad volumes, pointing to weakening business confidence and rising unemployment.

Morgan Stanley, in its 2027 outlook for the Australian economy released this week, expects sticky core inflation to keep the RBA cash rate on hold at 4.85% through the first half of 2027, before rising unemployment creates enough slack for two rate cuts before year’s end.

UBS is on the same page regarding the next rate cut – tipping November 2027. Its analysts believe rates may ease 50 basis points from there, but they caution that risks are now shifting towards an earlier or larger round of cuts, given the sharper-than-expected housing downturn and rapidly weakening consumer and business sentiment.

What to watch next

Today's data is a sobering reminder that the economy is entering a dangerous phase – inflation still well above the RBA's 2–3% target, a labour market shedding jobs, and growth slowing. UBS expects October's monthly CPI to show headline inflation at a new cycle high of 4.7% year-on-year, suggesting the inflation picture is likely to worsen still.

That CPI print is due on 25 November (next Wednesday), and markets will be watching it closely. Then, we’ll have the RBA's December meeting on 8 December and November's Labour Force data on 17 December to round out the year. A third consecutive fall of the size seen in September and October would certainly get the RBA’s attention – and would make it harder for Treasurer Jim Chalmers to argue, as he did after September’s numbers, that the labour market “remains resilient and one of our greatest strengths”.

References: This article draws on the ABS Labour Force, Australia, October 2026 release (19 November 2026) and the ABS Labour Force, Australia, September 2026 release (15 October 2026); ASX announcements from Nick Scali (Trading Update and 1H FY27 Profit Guidance, 21 October 2026), JB Hi-Fi (FY27 Sales Update, 29 October 2026) and Eagers Automotive (Trading Update, 5 November 2026); and broker research from Macquarie (Australian Wages Growth, 18 November 2026; Australian job ad volumes, 18 November 2026), Morgan Stanley (2027 Australia Macro+ Outlook, 16 November 2026) and UBS (Australian Economic Comment, 10 and 13 November 2026).

data.title: Singapore Dollar Consolidates, but May Be Weighed by Fed Rate-Hike Expectations — Market Talk
data.description: The Singapore dollar consolidates against its U.S. counterpart in the Asian session, but might be weighed by expectations for Fed rate hikes that tend to enhance the appeal of U.S. fixed-income assets and demand for the greenback. "Fed Governor Waller argued that the Fed should either raise rates by 50 bps in December or deliver a 25bp move and clearly signal another hike in January," two strategists at OCBC Group Research say in a report. "The October FOMC minutes reinforced the hawkish message," the strategists add. The U.S. dollar is steady at 1.2895 Singapore dollars, LSEG data show. (ronnie.harui@wsj.com)

data.title: Singapore Tourism Likely to Stay Weak This Year — Market Talk
data.description: Singapore's tourism is likely to remain weak in 2026 despite arrivals picking up in October for the first time since March, analysts at BMI, a unit of Fitch Solutions, say in a note. Citing the Singapore Tourism Board, they say the number of tourists visiting Singapore increased 0.5% on year to 1.39 million in October. From April to September, the number of tourists declined from a year earlier. A modest increase in October, combined with the weaker performance in the previous months, reinforces BMI's view that arrival growth is likely to be muted through year-end. (amanda.lee@wsj.com)

data.title: Australia's Job Market In Worse State Than Thought — Market Talk
data.description: After five interest rate increases this year by the Reserve Bank of Australia, economists have been waiting for the economy to break. With unemployment jumping to its highest level since 2021 in October, it was more of a crack than a snap. The job market looks worse than what the RBA anticipated, says Taylor Nugent, economist at NAB. The trend in employment growth is now just 7,000 per month, well below what is required to keep up with population growth, he says. NAB is forecasting a peak in the unemployment rate of 5.5%, compared to the RBA's forecast of 5.1%. (james.glynn@wsj.com; @JamesGlynnWSJ)
